summary: The authentication module contains critical vulnerabilities including SQL injection, hardcoded secrets, plaintext password comparison, and missing null/exception handling.

findings.title: SQL Injection in findUser
findings.body: User input is directly concatenated into the SQL query string in findUser, allowing arbitrary SQL execution and authentication bypass.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements (e.g. db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1', [username])) instead of string concatenation.

findings.title: Plaintext Password Comparison and Potential Null Dereference
findings.body: Passwords are verified via loose equality against unhashed values without constant-time comparison. Additionally, if findUser returns null or undefined for non-existent users, accessing user.password will throw an unhandled TypeError.
findings.recommendation: Check if user exists before accessing properties, store password hashes using a secure algorithm such as argon2 or bcrypt, and verify using timing-safe comparison functions.

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT Secret
findings.body: The JWT signing secret is hardcoded in source code, exposing cryptographic keys if the repository is shared or accessed.
findings.recommendation: Load the JWT secret from environment variables or a secure key management system (e.g. process.env.JWT_SECRET).

findings.title: Unhandled JSON.parse Exception in parseSession
findings.body: Calling JSON.parse directly on raw input without error handling will crash the execution context if invalid JSON is provided.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try-catch block to handle malformed input gracefully and validate session object structure.

samples.summary: The authentication module introduces critical SQL injection, hardcoded secrets, and unhandled null and parsing exceptions.

findings.title: SQL Injection in findUser query
findings.body: The findUser function concatenates the untrusted username parameter directly into the SQL query string, allowing arbitrary SQL injection and database compromise.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements (e.g., db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [username])).

findings.title: Unchecked user lookup result causes unhandled TypeError
findings.body: If findUser returns null or undefined for nonexistent users, accessing user.password will throw an unhandled TypeError and crash the authentication flow.
findings.recommendation: Check if user exists and verify password using a secure hash comparison (e.g., if (user && await bcrypt.compare(password, user.passwordHash))).

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT secret key
findings.body: JWT_SECRET is hardcoded in source control, allowing anyone with repository access to forge valid JWT authentication tokens.
findings.recommendation: Retrieve the JWT secret from environment variables or a secrets manager (e.g., process.env.JWT_SECRET) and ensure it is properly validated on startup.

findings.title: Unhandled JSON.parse exception in parseSession
findings.body: Calling JSON.parse directly on untrusted raw input without a try/catch block will throw a SyntaxError on malformed input.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try/catch block or helper to safely handle malformed input and return null or an error.

samples.summary: Critical security vulnerabilities including SQL injection and hardcoded secrets, alongside missing error and null checks, require remediation.

findings.title: SQL Injection via Unsanitized Concatenation
findings.body: The username parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL query in findUser, enabling arbitrary SQL injection that can lead to authentication bypass or data leakage.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries (e.g. `db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [username])`).

findings.title: Unchecked User Existence Before Password Access
findings.body: If findUser returns null or undefined for an unknown username, accessing user.password will throw an unhandled TypeError and crash the request.
findings.recommendation: Verify that user exists before inspecting properties (e.g., `if (user && user.password ...)`).

findings.title: Plaintext Password Comparison and Loose Equality
findings.body: Passwords are evaluated in plaintext using loose equality (`==`) rather than a secure, constant-time password hashing and verification function (e.g. bcrypt/argon2).
findings.recommendation: Store and verify password hashes using an algorithm like bcrypt or argon2.

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT Secret
findings.body: JWT_SECRET is hardcoded in the source file, which exposes the signing key and prevents environment-specific rotation.
findings.recommendation: Load the JWT secret from environment variables (e.g. `process.env.JWT_SECRET`).

findings.title: Unhandled SyntaxError in JSON Parsing
findings.body: parseSession calls JSON.parse on raw input without error handling, which throws an unhandled SyntaxError if invalid JSON is provided.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try/catch block and handle invalid input gracefully.
